title: Algebraic and affinoid completed local rings at closed points
statement:
Let $F$ be a complete field with a nontrivial real-valued nonarchimedean absolute value. For $n\ge0$, write $P=F[T_1,\ldots,T_n]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] and let $J\subseteq P$ be an ideal. Let $F\langle T_1,\ldots,T_nangle$ be the ring of restricted series $\sum_{
u\in\mathbf N^n}a_
u T^
u$, meaning that for every $\epsilon>0$ only finitely many coefficients satisfy $|a_
u|\ge\epsilon$, with Gauss norm $\sup_
u|a_
u|$. Put $B=P/J$ and $C=F\langle Tangle/JF\langle Tangle$, with the quotient seminorm. The ideal $JF\langle Tangle$ is closed, and $C$ is a Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] complete normed $F$-algebra for this quotient norm (the zero algebra is allowed). For every maximal ideal $\mathfrak m\subset C$, its inverse image $\mathfrak p$ under $B	o C$ is maximal, and the induced local map $B_{\mathfrak p}	o C_{\mathfrak m}$ gives an isomorphism $\widehat{B_{\mathfrak p}}\xrightarrow{\sim}\widehat{C_{\mathfrak m}}$ of completions at their respective maximal ideals [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime, def-weil-pbc-adic-completion].

source.place: Theorem 3.5.5 Step 3, printed p. 22: the isomorphism between completed local rings of B=A tensor_V Khat and C=Ahat[1/pi] at maximal points; Tate algebra Noetherianity and closed ideals are the analytic prerequisites of this comparison.
